audit.whatIsWrong: TRICKY 7/10 is defensible on the early lane but the prose never said why, and every 'he/his' in it pointed at a female enemy.
audit.why: The whole difficulty is range: Light Binding 1175, Prismatic Barrier 1150, Lucent Singularity 1100, all against an 850 Q and a 700 Twin Fang on a champion with no dash and no boots. That is a farm-and-survive lane until 6, which is exactly what the win rate of 53.03% over 841 games reflects — she owns early, you own everything after.
audit.corrected: Rating kept; the early fields now carry the actual range numbers, and every pronoun is corrected.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer read 'Skill' on all seven rows while the content layer read Lux/Lux/Skill/Cassiopeia x4 and matched the packet levelChart. Every full-layer why was the generic Cassiopeia template regardless of the row.
audit.why: A flat 'Skill' chart on a lane this stage-dependent tells the reader nothing, and it contradicts the other layer on six of seven rows.
audit.corrected: Moved rows 0-1 to Lux and rows 3-6 to Cassiopeia, leaving row 2 as Skill, and rewrote the whys on the rows that changed verdict. win[0..6] already hold these values on disk, so there is no paired content edit to write — before would equal after — and both layers now agree on all seven rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page leaned on Miasma as an anti-dive and gank-closer ('your W makes every gank a guaranteed kill', 'the next engage arrives ungrounded'). Lux has no dash, blink or movement ability at all, so the grounding half of Miasma does nothing in this matchup. Prismatic Barrier was never mentioned in any trading field, and Illumination's auto-attack detonation (missingInteractions) appeared nowhere.
audit.why: Grounding advice against a champion with nothing to ground is filler dressed as a mechanic, and it displaces the interactions that do decide the lane: the Final Spark wind-up your R punishes, and a shield that eats one burst but not a Twin Fang stream.
audit.corrected: Replaced the grounding claims with Lux's actual constraint (no dash to leave with), put Final Spark's stationary cast into dosFull[1].d and phases[4].why, Prismatic Barrier into dontsFull[2].d and breakdown.carry, and Illumination into dosFull[2].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit (lint) and told the reader to 'minion-block' Light Binding without saying the root stops on the first two units it touches.
audit.why: That is the single most useful fact in the matchup and it was stated as a vague instruction instead of a mechanic.
audit.corrected: Light Binding 10s flat at 1175 and binds up to two units, Lucent Singularity 10s at rank 1, Final Spark 60/50/40.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim, dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim, dontsFull[1].d was the anti-dive Miasma line under a title about defensive Petrifying Gaze (lint). whys[3] sits on the Levels 4-5 row but its text says 'once you hit 6'.
audit.why: Bodies contradicted titles, and one why described a different stage than its own row.
audit.corrected: All four rewritten to their own subject.

notes: The packet's suspectNames are false positives on all three: 'Lucent Singularity-' is the correct name with a hyphen from the combo notation, and 'Your Petrifying Gaze' is the correct name with a possessive in front. I still rewrote whys[3], but for a different reason — it sits on the Levels 4-5 row and its text said 'once you hit 6', describing the wrong stage. The bigger finding is the Miasma grounding advice: Lux has no dash, blink or movement ability, so 'ground every gank', 'the next engage arrives ungrounded' and 'your W makes every gank a guaranteed kill' were all inert here. I fixed the ones I rewrote; breakdown.mid still says 'ground every gank' and report[10].t still says 'ground Lux's escape', both templates I could not ground in this kit — reported in sectionsMissing rather than replaced with an invention.
